name: Data Analyst
description: Entry-level data analyst turning raw data into clear, correct answers with SQL, Python and charts.

skills.name: SQL for Analysis
skills.description: Querying relational data for answers: joins, aggregation, window functions and clean results.

L1: Names the exact tables, queries and schema used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains what an index speeds up and what it costs on writes
Explains the difference between INNER and LEFT JOIN with an example
Explains what a transaction guarantees (atomicity, isolation) and a bug it prevents
L3: Explains when they would denormalize or NOT add an index, and the trade-off
Defends SQL vs a document store for their data with a real cost of each
Explains how they found and fixed a slow query (EXPLAIN, index, rewrite)

skills.name: Python for Data
skills.description: Working with data in Python: pandas, cleaning, merging, and reproducible notebooks.

L1: Names the exact libraries, datasets and steps used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains how a merge or join can silently duplicate rows and how to check
Explains the difference between a view and a copy in pandas or a similar gotcha
Explains how they made the notebook reproducible
L3: Explains when they would NOT use pandas (data too large, SQL is better) and what they use instead
Defends a cleaning decision against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: Data Preparation
skills.description: Finding and fixing problems in data: missing values, duplicates, outliers, types and bias in collection.

L1: Names the exact data problems found and how each was handled used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains at least two ways to handle missing data and what each does to the result
Explains how an outlier changes the mean and the median
Explains how they checked the data was correct before analysing
L3: Explains when they would NOT drop or impute a value and the bias that could introduce
Defends a cleaning rule against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: Statistics & Probability
skills.description: Descriptive statistics, distributions, sampling, correlation and basic hypothesis testing.

L1: Names the exact statistical measures or tests applied used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains what a p-value does and does not say
Explains why correlation is not causation with an example
Explains how sample size affects a confidence interval
L3: Explains when they would NOT trust a result (small sample, bias, multiple tests) and what they would do
Defends the test or measure chosen against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: Visualization & Storytelling
skills.description: Choosing the right chart, avoiding misleading visuals and communicating a finding to a decision maker.

L1: Names the exact charts and the question each answered used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains which chart fits a comparison, a trend, a distribution and a part-to-whole, and why
Explains one way a chart can mislead (truncated axis, dual axis)
Explains how they tailored the message for a non-technical reader
L3: Explains when they would NOT use a chart and show a table or a single number
Defends a chart choice against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: Business Metrics & Analysis
skills.description: Turning a business question into a metric, a query and a recommendation.

L1: Names the exact question, metric and decision used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains how they defined the metric and its denominator
Explains the difference between a leading and a lagging indicator
Explains how they checked the result against the business context
L3: Explains when they would NOT act on the number and what they would check first
Defends a metric choice against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each
